page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-60 is a General Purpose virtual machine powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 processors built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provisions 60 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core (60 vCPUs), omitting simultaneous multithreading (SMT). It is equipped with 240.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster, alongside architectural flags such as AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, and FMA. There are no bundled GPUs, no local NVMe storage arrays, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included in the baseline configuration.

Benchmark results highlight strong multithreaded compute capability, driven by the absence of core sharing or hyperthreading contention. In the stress-ng multi-core CPU benchmark, the instance places in the top 10% with a score of 141,982.77, while its single-core stress-ng performance sits in the top 25% at 2,693.79. It achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,297.0 and excels in parallelized execution, demonstrating top 25% results in Clang software compilation (54,068.0) and ray tracing (75,478.0). PassMark benchmarks confirm this profile with strong rankings in overall CPU (76,182.72), extended instructions (88,572.12), encryption (66,859.44), and memory (2,944.68).

Memory bandwidth measurements demonstrate 6,846.14 GB/sec on cached 16 KB small blocks (top 25%), though throughput moderates to middle-tier levels of 141.75 GB/sec for uncached read blocks (256 MB) and 64.61 GB/sec for uncached writes. Similarly, standard web serving throughput reaches 24.96 GB/sec (average tier), and single-threaded operations such as gzip compression (25.32 GB/sec) and Geekbench single-core execution (1,601.0) maintain average performance. The absence of AVX-512 extensions and dedicated accelerators creates tradeoffs for large model execution, evidenced by weak large LLM text generation at 2.56 tokens per second.

The t2d-standard-60 offers strong multi-core cost efficiency by delivering 60 full physical cores without SMT thread degradation. It is well matched for horizontally scalable enterprise applications, high-concurrency microservices, PassMark database operations (26,072.24), in-memory data structures like Redis (86.31 million SET ops/sec), continuous integration test suites, and batch multithreaded decompression tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-60 is a General Purpose server offering 60 dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 physical cores (60 vCPUs with 1 thread per core) on the x86_64 architecture and 240.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core). It contains no integrated GPU accelerators and relies entirely on external storage. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core compute capability, achieving 141,982.77 in stress-ng multi-core tests, a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,297.0, and 86.31 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 6,846.14 GB/sec for cached 16 KB blocks, though uncached large blocks perform within average thresholds. Due to its dedicated physical core layout, the instance provides reliable scaling without thread contention, making it appropriate for large-scale CI/CD compilation, high-concurrency container deployments, database operations, and data analytics pipelines.
